question.prompt: A list of \(2018\) positive integers has a unique mode, which occurs exactly \(10\) times. What is the least number of distinct values that can occur in the list?

solutions.title: Bound the frequencies and construct a list
solutions.explanation:
Because the mode is unique and appears exactly \(10\) times, every other value can appear at most \(9\) times.

Removing the mode's entries leaves
\[
2018-10=2008
\]
entries. If these used at most \(223\) distinct values, they could contain at most
\[
223\cdot9=2007
\]
entries, which is one too few. Thus at least \(224\) distinct values besides the mode are needed, giving at least \(225\) distinct values altogether.

To attain this bound, take nine copies of each integer from \(1\) through \(223\), ten copies of \(224\), and one copy of \(225\). This gives
\[
223\cdot9+10+1=2018
\]
entries and exactly \(225\) distinct values. Only \(224\) occurs ten times, so it is the unique mode.

The least number is therefore \(\boxed{225}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
